hypotheses.name: Genuine Hawk
hypotheses.description: Warsh truly believes in fighting inflation and the 2% target. His rhetoric is not theater. Balance sheet shrinks aggressively. QT continues. Rates stay higher for longer.
confirming_signals: Balance sheet panel recommends aggressive QT with explicit size targets
Warsh raises rates or holds firm despite political pressure
Warsh maintains pure hawkish stance for 12+ months
denying_signals: Warsh pivots to 'ample reserves' language without targets
QT slows or pauses before balance sheet reaches targets
Any rate cut within 6 months despite hawkish rhetoric

hypotheses.name: Pantomime (Hawkish Talk, Dovish Action)
hypotheses.description: Warsh was appointed to SOUND hawkish while DOING dovish. Shadow easing through reserves management, expanded repo, slowed QT. The hawkish rhetoric provides political cover.
confirming_signals: Balance sheet panel recommends 'ample reserves' without targets
Reserves management purchases expand and become permanent
Warsh's language shifts from 'fighting inflation' to 'sustaining expansion'
denying_signals: Warsh raises rates or tightens policy materially
Inflation drops below 2.5% AND Warsh still holds rates

hypotheses.name: Transition (Hawkish Now, Dovish Later)
hypotheses.description: Warsh starts hawkish to establish credibility and independence. Over 6-12 months, fiscal reality + political pressure + AI capex needs force a pragmatic pivot. The 2% target becomes fiction. Inflation drifts to 3-3.5% through tolerance.
confirming_signals: Balance sheet panel recommends gradual QT with 'flexible' framework
Warsh's language gradually softens over 3-6 months
Reserves management purchases start small but grow
Rate hold language shifts from 'higher for longer' to 'patient'
denying_signals: Warsh maintains pure hawkish stance for 12+ months
No expansion of reserves management purchases
Warsh explicitly rules out any form of QE or easing
hypotheses.curve_implication: 2s10s flat at +30-50 for 3-6mo, then steepens to +60-100

signals.description: Warsh's first congressional testimony: defended 2% target, criticized past Chairs, pledged 'regime change'. Markets initially rallied day after appointment (calling bluff) but Warsh doubled down.
Warsh assembled balance sheet review panel — provides institutional cover for eventual policy pivot. Deliberately ambiguous 'regime change' language could mean tighter OR restructured.
Trump's DOJ investigation of Powell for not cutting rates shows Trump demands dovish policy. Warsh was appointed to replace the non-compliant Chair.
Curve stable at 2s10s +40bps over 30 days. Bond market has NOT priced in any scenario shift. All yields rose 13bps in parallel (inflation expectations up) but shape unchanged.
